arxiv-1801-03257.title: Translating Pro-Drop Languages with Reconstruction Models
arxiv-1801-03257.creator: Longyue Wang, Zhaopeng Tu, Shuming Shi, Tong Zhang, Yvette Graham, Qun Liu
arxiv-1801-03257.description: Abstract Pronouns are frequently omitted in pro-drop languages, such as Chinese, generally leading to significant challenges with respect to the production of complete translations. To date, very little attention has been paid to the dropped pronoun (DP) problem within neural machine translation (NMT). In this work, we propose a novel reconstruction-based approach to alleviating DP translation problems for NMT models.

arxiv-2306-11732.title: Retrieving-to-Answer: Zero-Shot Video Question Answering with Frozen Large Language Models
arxiv-2306-11732.creator: Junting Pan, Ziyi Lin, Yuying Ge, Xiatian Zhu, Renrui Zhang, Yi Wang, Yu Qiao, Hongsheng Li
arxiv-2306-11732.description: Abstract Video Question Answering (VideoQA) has been significantly advanced from the scaling of recent Large Language Models (LLMs). The key idea is to convert the visual information into the language feature space so that the capacity of LLMs can be fully exploited.

arxiv-2310-08753.title: CompA: Addressing the Gap in Compositional Reasoning in Audio-Language Models
arxiv-2310-08753.creator: Sreyan Ghosh, Ashish Seth, Sonal Kumar, Utkarsh Tyagi, Chandra Kiran Evuru, S. Ramaneswaran S. Sakshi Oriol Nieto Ramani Duraiswami Dinesh Manocha
arxiv-2310-08753.description: Abstract A fundamental characteristic of audio is its compositional nature. Audio-language models (ALMs) trained using a contrastive approach (e.g., CLAP) that learns a shared representation between audio and language modalities have improved performance in many downstream applications, including zero-shot audio classification, audio retrieval, etc.

arxiv-2411-08508.title: BillBoard Splatting (BBSplat): Learnable Textured Primitives for Novel View Synthesis
arxiv-2411-08508.creator: David Svitov, Pietro Morerio, Lourdes Agapito, Alessio Del Bue
arxiv-2411-08508.description: Abstract We present billboard Splatting (BBSplat) - a novel approach for novel view synthesis based on textured geometric primitives. BBSplat represents the scene as a set of optimizable textured planar primitives with learnable RGB textures and alpha-maps to control their shape. BBSplat primitives can be used in any Gaussian Splatting pipeline as drop-in replacements for Gaussians.

arxiv-2511-15226.title: Frustration indices of signed subcubic graphs
arxiv-2511-15226.creator: Sirui Chen, Jiaao Li, Zhouningxin Wang
arxiv-2511-15226.description: Abstract The frustration index of a signed graph is defined as the minimum number of negative edges among all switching-equivalent signatures. This can be regarded as a generalization of the classical Max-Cut problem in graphs, as the Max-Cut problem is equivalent to determining the frustration index of signed graphs with all edges being negative signs.

pmc-13261663.title: ProtoCloud: A prototypical self-explaining model for single-cell analysis
pmc-13261663.creator: Kaiyun Guo, Jiarui Ding
pmc-13261663.description: SummaryCell type annotation is a fundamental task in single-cell genomics. Although various methods have been developed for automatic annotation, they often function as black-box models lacking explainability, proper uncertainty estimation, and robustness for rare cell types. We introduce ProtoCloud, a self-explanatory deep generative model that embeds cells into a structured, low-dimensional space organized around cell-type-specific prototypes.

pmc-13610018.creator: Stefano Benvenuti
pmc-13610018.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Urbanization is widely recognized as a major driver of biodiversity loss; however, cities can also provide important refuges for pollinators when diverse and continuous floral resources are available. This study assessed the diversity of spontaneous insect-pollinated flora and its associated pollinator communities across five major urban habitat types (grasslands, road verges, artificial surfaces, wooded areas, and wetlands) in the Mediterranean cities of Pisa, Livorno, and Lucca (central Italy).
